You are zesty_lantern63, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_1 with gentle_otter27, pale_lantern48, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

## Task context
Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll take the initial pass on the executable’s CLI and docs, then share an overview with the group and pick an uncovered behavior area to implement.

--- rtk filters and compresses command outputs before they reach your LLM context. Single Rust binary, 100+ supported commands, <10ms overhead. ## Token Savings (30-min Claude Code Session) | Operation | Frequency | Standard | rtk | Savings | |-----------|-----------|----------|-----|---------| | `ls` / `tree` | 10x | 2,000 | 400 | -80% | | `cat` / `read` | 20x | 40,000 | 12,000 | -70% | | `grep` / `rg` | 8x | 16,000 | 3,200 | -80% | | `git status` | 10x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% | | `git diff` | 5x | 10,000 | 2,500 | -75% | | `git log` | 5x | 2,500 | 500 | -80% | | `git add/commit/push` | 8x | 1,600 | 120 | -92% | | `cargo test` / `npm test` | 5x | 25,000 | 2,500 | -90% | | `ruff check` | 3x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% | | `pytest` | 4x | 8,000 | 800 | -90% | | `go test` | 3x | 6,000 | 600 | -90% | | `docker ps` | 3x | 900 | 180 | -80% | | **Total** | | **~118,000** | **~23,900** | **-80%** | > Estimates based on medium-sized TypeScript/Rust projects. Actual savings vary by project size. ## Installation ### Homebrew (recommended) ```bash brew install rtk ``` ### Quick Install (Linux/macOS) ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh ``` > Installs to `~/.local/bin`. Add to PATH if needed: > ```bash > echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc # or ~/.zshrc > ``` ### Cargo ```bash cargo install --git https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk ``` ### Pre-built Binaries Download from [releases](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/releases): - macOS: `rtk-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - Linux: `rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` - Windows: `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` > **Windows users**: Extract the zip and place `rtk.exe` somewhere in your PATH (e.g. `C:\Users\\.local\bin`). Run RTK from **Command Prompt**, **PowerShell**, or **Windows Terminal** — do not double-click the `.exe` (it will flash and close). For the best experience, use [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) where the full hook system works natively. See [Windows setup](#windows) below for details. ### Verify Installation ```bash rtk --version # Should show "rtk 0.28.2" rtk gain # Should show token savings stats ``` > **Name collision warning**: Another project named "rtk" (Rust Type Kit) exists on crates.io. If `rtk gain` fails, you have the wrong package. Use `cargo install --git` above instead. ## Quick Start ```bash # 1. Install for your AI tool rtk init -g # Claude Code / Copilot (default) rtk init -g --gemini # Gemini CLI rtk init -g --codex # Codex (OpenAI) rtk init -g --agent cursor # Cursor rtk init --agent windsurf # Windsurf rtk init --agent cline # Cline / Roo Code rtk init --agent kilocode # Kilo Code rtk init --agent antigravity # Google Antigravity rtk init --agent hermes # Hermes # 2. Restart your AI tool, then test git status # Automatically rewritten to rtk git status ``` Hook-based agents rewrite Bash commands (e.g., `git status` -> `rtk git status`) before execution. Plugin-based agents, including Hermes, use their plugin API to rewrite commands before execution. The agent receives compact output without needing to call `rtk` explicitly. **Important:** the hook only runs on Bash tool calls. Claude Code built-in tools like `Read`, `Grep`, and `Glob` do not pass through the Bash hook, so they are not auto-rewritten. Removes noise (comments, whitespace, boilerplate) 2. **Grouping** - Aggregates similar items (files by directory, errors by type) 3. **Truncation** - Keeps relevant context, cuts redundancy 4. **Deduplication** - Collapses repeated log lines with counts ## Commands ### Files ```bash rtk ls . # Token-optimized directory tree rtk read file.rs # Smart file reading rtk read file.rs -l aggressive # Signatures only (strips bodies) rtk smart file.rs # 2-line heuristic code summary rtk find "*.rs" . # Compact find results rtk grep "pattern" . # Grouped search results rtk diff file1 file2 # Condensed diff ``` ### Git ```bash rtk git status # Compact status rtk git log -n 10 # One-line commits rtk git diff # Condensed diff rtk git add # -> "ok" rtk git commit -m "msg" # -> "ok abc1234" rtk git push # -> "ok main" rtk git pull # -> "ok 3 files +10 -2" ``` ### GitHub CLI ```bash rtk gh pr list # Compact PR listing rtk gh pr view 42 # PR details + checks rtk gh issue list # Compact issue listing rtk gh run list # Workflow run status ``` ### Test Runners ```bash rtk jest # Jest compact (failures only) rtk vitest # Vitest compact (failures only) rtk playwright test # E2E results (failures only) rtk pytest # Python tests (-90%) rtk go test # Go tests (NDJSON, -90%) rtk cargo test # Cargo tests (-90%) rtk rake test # Ruby minitest (-90%) rtk rspec # RSpec tests (JSON, -60%+) rtk err # Filter errors only from any command rtk test # Generic test wrapper - failures only (-90%) ``` ### Build & Lint ```bash rtk lint # ESLint grouped by rule/file rtk lint biome # Supports other linters rtk tsc # TypeScript errors grouped by file rtk next build # Next.js build compact rtk prettier --check . # Files needing formatting rtk cargo build # Cargo build (-80%) rtk cargo clippy # Cargo clippy (-80%) rtk ruff check # Python linting (JSON, -80%) rtk golangci-lint run # Go linting (JSON, -85%) rtk rubocop # Ruby linting (JSON, -60%+) ``` ### Package Managers ```bash rtk pnpm list # Compact dependency tree rtk pip list # Python packages (auto-detect uv) rtk pip outdated # Outdated packages rtk bundle install # Ruby gems (strip Using lines) rtk prisma generate # Schema generation (no ASCII art) ``` ### AWS ```bash rtk aws sts get-caller-identity # One-line identity rtk aws ec2 describe-instances # Compact instance list rtk aws lambda list-functions # Name/runtime/memory (strips secrets) rtk aws logs get-log-events # Timestamped messages only rtk aws cloudformation describe-stack-events # Failures first rtk aws dynamodb scan # Unwraps type annotations rtk aws iam list-roles # Strips policy documents rtk aws s3 ls # Truncated with tee recovery ``` "}

+

+

+def _cargo(s):
+    lines = s.splitlines()
+    failures = []
+    warnings = []
+    summary = []
+    for line in lines:
+        if "warning:" in line.lower(): warnings.append(line)
+        if re.search(r"test result:.*FAILED", line): summary.append(line)
+        if re.search(r"\bFAILED\b", line) and not line.startswith("test result:"):
+            failures.append(line)
+        if line.startswith("error:") or line.startswith("error["):
+            failures.append(line)
+    if not failures and not summary:
+        return "No tests failed" if "test result:" in s else s
+    out = [f"cargo test: {len(failures)} errors, {len(warnings)} warnings (0 crates)", "═══════════════════════════════════════"]
+    out += warnings
+    if warnings and failures: out.append("")
+    out += [f"{i}. {line}" for i, line in enumerate(failures, 1)]
+    out += summary
+    return "\n".join(out)
+
+
+def _pytest(s):
+    lines = s.splitlines()
+    summary = next((x.strip() for x in reversed(lines) if re.search(r"\d+ passed|\d+ failed|\d+ error", x)), "")
+    if not summary:
+        return "Pytest: No tests collected" if "no tests ran" in s.lower() or not s.strip() else s
+    failures = []
+    in_fail = False
+    current = []
+    for line in lines:
+        if "FAILURES" in line and set(line.strip()) <= {"=", " "}: in_fail = True
+        elif in_fail and line.startswith("___"):
+            if current: failures.append(current)
+            current = [line.strip(" _")]
+        elif in_fail and line.startswith("==="): in_fail = False

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Small independent implementation of the RTK command interface."""
import os
import re
import shlex
import sys

VERSION = "0.42.0"

HELP = '''A high-performance CLI proxy designed to filter and summarize system outputs before they reach your LLM context.

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  ls             List directory contents with token-optimized output (proxy to native ls)
  tree           Directory tree with token-optimized output
  read           Read file with intelligent filtering
  smart          Generate 2-line technical summary (heuristic-based)
  git            Git commands with compact output
  gh             GitHub CLI with token-optimized output
  err            Run command and show only errors/warnings
  test           Run tests and show only failures
  json           Show JSON (compact values by default, or keys-only with --keys-only)
  deps           Summarize project dependencies
  env            Show environment variables (filtered, sensitive masked)
  find           Find files with compact tree output
  diff           Ultra-condensed diff (only changed lines)
  log            Filter and deduplicate log output
  wc             Word/line/byte count with compact output
  init           Initialize rtk instructions for assistant CLI usage
  gain           Show token savings summary and history
  config         Show or create configuration file
  rewrite        Rewrite a raw command to its RTK equivalent
  hook           Hook processors for Gemini CLI, Copilot, etc.
  run            Execute a shell command via sh -c (raw, no filtering or tracking)
  proxy          Execute command without filtering but track usage
  pipe           Read stdin, apply filter, print filtered output

Options:
  -v, --verbose...
      Verbosity level (-v, -vv, -vvv)
      --ultra-compact   Ultra-compact mode
      --skip-env        Set SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1 for child processes
  -h, --help            Print help
  -V, --version         Print version'''

def rewrite_one(text):
    """Rewrite the first executable word of shell command segments."""
    # Split on shell operators while preserving separators and quoting.
    pieces = re.split(r'((?:&&|\|\||[;|]\s*))', text)
    changed = False
    out = []
    for p in pieces:
        if not p or re.fullmatch(r'(?:&&|\|\||[;|]\s*)', p):
            out.append(p); continue
        lead = p[:len(p)-len(p.lstrip())]
        body = p[len(lead):]
        # Keep leading assignments and environment wrappers intact.
        try:
            toks = shlex.split(body, posix=True)
        except ValueError:
            toks = body.split()
        if not toks:
            out.append(p); continue
        n = 0
        prefix = []
        while n < len(toks) and (re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=', toks[n]) or toks[n] in ('sudo','env','command','time')):
            prefix.append(toks[n]); n += 1
        if n >= len(toks):
            out.append(p); continue
        cmd = toks[n]
        args = toks[n+1:]
        mapped = None
        if cmd == 'rtk':
            out.append(p); continue
        if cmd == 'cat':
            mapped = 'read'
        elif cmd in ('head','tail'):
            count = None
            rest = []
            i=0
            while i < len(args):
                a=args[i]
                if a in ('-n','--lines') and i+1<len(args): count=args[i+1]; i+=2; continue
                m=re.match(r'^-(\d+)$',a)
                if m: count=m.group(1)
                else: rest.append(a)
                i+=1
            if cmd=='head' and count is not None:
                mapped='read'; args=rest+['--max-lines',count]
            else: mapped='read'
        elif cmd == 'python' and len(args)>1 and args[0]=='-m' and args[1] in ('pytest','unittest'):
            mapped=args[1]; args=args[2:]
        elif cmd in ('pytest','ruff','mypy','cargo','go','npm','npx','pnpm','git','gh','glab','aws','psql','docker','kubectl','jest','vitest','tsc','next','prettier','playwright','pip','wget','curl','find','grep','ls','tree','wc','diff','rg','gradlew','ruby','bundle','rake','rspec','golangci-lint','dotnet','prisma'):
            mapped=cmd
            if cmd=='kubectl' and args[:2]==['get','pods']: args[1]='pods'
            if cmd=='npx' and args and args[0]=='tsc': mapped='tsc'; args=args[1:]
            elif cmd=='npx' and args and args[0] in ('eslint','prisma'): mapped=args[0]; args=args[1:]
            elif cmd=='python' and len(args)>0 and args[0]=='-m' and len(args)>1 and args[1] in ('pytest','unittest'):
                mapped=args[1]; args=args[2:]
        if mapped is None:
            out.append(p); continue
        # Construct a replacement command. The common form has one executable and
        # is reconstructed only when tokens can be safely re-quoted.
        newtokens = prefix + ['rtk', mapped] + args
        rendered = ' '.join(shlex.quote(x) for x in newtokens)
        # Preserve trailing whitespace; shell operators themselves are untouched.
        rendered += p[len(p.rstrip()):]
        out.append(lead + rendered)
        changed = True
    return ''.join(out), changed

def main(argv):
    if not argv or argv[0] in ('-h','--help','help'):
        if len(argv)>1 and argv[0]=='help':
            # General help is useful even for command-specific requests.
            pass
        print(HELP)
        return 0
    if argv[0] in ('-V','--version','version'):
        print('rtk '+VERSION); return 0
    if argv[0]=='rewrite':
        args=argv[1:]
        if args and args[0] in ('-h','--help'):
            print('Rewrite a raw command to its RTK equivalent (single source of truth for hooks)\n\nUsage: executable rewrite [OPTIONS] [ARGS...]'); return 0
        # Clap accepts either one string or an argument vector; vector is joined.
        cmd=' '.join(args)
        out,ok=rewrite_one(cmd)
        if ok:
            sys.stdout.write(out)
            return 3
        return 1
    if argv[0]=='run' and len(argv)>1:
        import subprocess
        return subprocess.call(argv[1:],shell=True)
    if argv[0]=='pipe':
        from pipe_impl import run_pipe
        return run_pipe(argv[1:])
    if argv[0] == 'read':
        from read_cmd import run_read
        return run_read(argv[1:])
    if argv[0] == 'grep':
        from grep_cmd import run_grep
        return run_grep(argv[1:])
    if argv[0] in ('env', 'wc'):
        from env_wc import env, wc
        if argv[0] == 'env':
            sys.stdout.write(env(argv[1:])); return 0
        out, err, rc = wc(argv[1:])
        sys.stdout.write(out); sys.stderr.write(err); return rc
    if argv[0] in ('log','diff'):
        from filters_extra import run_log, run_diff
        return run_log(argv[1:]) if argv[0]=='log' else run_diff(argv[1:])
    return 0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
"}

const patch="*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/wrapper_cmd.py
+"""Generic error-only and test-output wrappers."""
+import re
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+
+def _help(kind):
+    label = "Run command and show only errors/warnings" if kind == "err" else "Run tests and show only failures"
+    print(f"{label}\n\nUsage: executable {kind} [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]...\n\nArguments:\n  [COMMAND]...  Command to run\n\nOptions:\n  -v, --verbose...     Verbosity level (-v, -vv, -vvv)\n      --ultra-compact  Ultra-compact mode: ASCII icons, inline format (Level 2 optimizations)\n      --skip-env       Set SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1 for child processes (Next.js, tsc, lint, prisma)\n  -h, --help           Print help")
+
+
+def run_wrapper(kind, args):
+    if any(a in ("-h", "--help") for a in args):
+        _help(kind)
+        return 0
+    command = [a for a in args if a not in ("-v", "-vv", "-vvv", "--ultra-compact", "--skip-env")]
+    if not command:
+        print(f"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n  [COMMAND]...", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    proc = subprocess.run(" ".join(command), shell=True, text=True,
+                          stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
+    lines = (proc.stdout + proc.stderr).splitlines()
+    if kind == "err":
+        selected = [line for line in lines if re.search(r"\b(error|warning|warn|fatal|exception)\b", line, re.I)]
+        if selected: sys.stdout.write("\n".join(selected) + "\n")
+    else:
+        selected = [line for line in lines if re.search(r"\b(fail(?:ed|ure)?|error|panic|assert(?:ion)?)\b", line, re.I)]
+        if not selected:
+            selected = [line for line in lines if re.search(r"\b\d+\s+(?:passed|failed|tests?\s+passed)\b|test result:", line, re.I)]
+        if selected:
+            print("OUTPUT (last 5 lines):")
+            for line in selected[-5:]: print("  " + line)
+            print()
+    return proc.returncode
*** End Patch";
const r=await tools.apply_patch(patch);text(r)

def rewrite_one(text):
    """Rewrite the first executable word of shell command segments."""
    # Split on shell operators while preserving separators and quoting.
    pieces = re.split(r'((?:&&|\|\||[;|]\s*))', text)
    changed = False
    out = []
    for p in pieces:
        if not p or re.fullmatch(r'(?:&&|\|\||[;|]\s*)', p):
            out.append(p); continue
        lead = p[:len(p)-len(p.lstrip())]
        body = p[len(lead):]
        # Keep leading assignments and environment wrappers intact.
        try:
            toks = shlex.split(body, posix=True)
        except ValueError:
            toks = body.split()
        if not toks:
            out.append(p); continue
        n = 0
        prefix = []
        while n < len(toks) and (re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=', toks[n]) or toks[n] in ('sudo','env','command','time')):
            prefix.append(toks[n]); n += 1
        if n >= len(toks):
            out.append(p); continue
        cmd = toks[n]
        args = toks[n+1:]
        mapped = None
        if cmd == 'rtk':
            out.append(p); continue
        if cmd == 'cat':
            mapped = 'read'
        elif cmd in ('head','tail'):
            count = None
            rest = []
            i=0
            while i < len(args):
                a=args[i]
                m=re.match(r'^-(\d+)$',a)
                if m: count=m.group(1)
                elif cmd=='tail' and a in ('-n','--lines') and i+1<len(args): count=args[i+1]; i+=2; continue
                else: rest.append(a)
                i+=1

def rewrite_one(text):
    """Rewrite the first executable word of shell command segments."""
    # Split on shell operators while preserving separators and quoting.
    pieces = re.split(r'((?:&&|\|\||[;|]\s*))', text)
    changed = False
    out = []
    for p in pieces:
        if not p or re.fullmatch(r'(?:&&|\|\||[;|]\s*)', p):
            out.append(p); continue
        lead = p[:len(p)-len(p.lstrip())]
        body = p[len(lead):]
        # Keep leading assignments and environment wrappers intact.
        try:
            toks = shlex.split(body, posix=True)
        except ValueError:
            toks = body.split()
        if not toks:
            out.append(p); continue
        n = 0
        prefix = []
        while n < len(toks) and (re.match(r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=', toks[n]) or toks[n] in ('sudo','env','command','time')):
            prefix.append(toks[n]); n += 1
        if n >= len(toks):
            out.append(p); continue
        cmd = toks[n]
        args = toks[n+1:]
        mapped = None
        if cmd == 'rtk':
            out.append(p); continue
        if cmd == 'cat':
            mapped = 'read'
        elif cmd in ('head','tail'):
            count = None
            rest = []
            i=0
            while i < len(args):
                a=args[i]
                m=re.match(r'^-(\d+)$',a)
                if m: count=m.group(1)
                elif cmd=='tail' and a in ('-n','--lines') and i+1<len(args): count=args[i+1]; i+=2; continue
                else: rest.append(a)
                i+=1
            if cmd=='head' and count is not None:
                mapped='read'; args=rest+['--max-lines',count]
            elif cmd=='tail' and count is not None:
                mapped='read'; args=rest+['--tail-lines',count]
            elif cmd=='head' and args:
                pass
            elif cmd=='tail' and args:
                mapped='read'
        elif cmd == 'python' and len(args)>1 and args[0]=='-m' and args[1] in ('pytest','unittest'):
            mapped=args[1]; args=args[2:]
        elif cmd in ('pytest','ruff','mypy','cargo','go','make','npm','npx','pnpm','git','gh','glab','aws','psql','docker','kubectl','jest','vitest','tsc','next','prettier','playwright','pip','wget','curl','find','grep','ls','tree','wc','diff','rg','gradlew','ruby','bundle','rake','rspec','golangci-lint','dotnet','prisma'):
            mapped=cmd
            if cmd=='kubectl' and args[:2]==['get','pods']: args[1]='pods'
            if cmd == 'rg': mapped='grep'
            if cmd == 'npm' and (not args or args[0] != 'run'): mapped=None
            if cmd == 'pnpm' and (not args or args[0] not in ('install','list','add','remove','update','outdated')): mapped=None
            if cmd=='npx' and args and args[0]=='tsc': mapped='tsc'; args=args[1:]
            elif cmd=='npx' and args and args[0]=='eslint': mapped='lint'; args=args[1:]
            elif cmd=='npx' and args and args[0]=='prisma': mapped='prisma'; args=args[1:]
            elif cmd=='python' and len(args)>0 and args[0]=='-m' and len(args)>1 and args[1] in ('pytest','unittest'):
                mapped=args[1]; args=args[2:]
        if mapped is None:
            out.append(p); continue
        # Construct a replacement command. The common form has one executable and
        # is reconstructed only when tokens can be safely re-quoted.
        newtokens = prefix + ['rtk', mapped] + args
        rendered = ' '.join(shlex.quote(x) for x in newtokens)
        # Preserve trailing whitespace; shell operators themselves are untouched.
        rendered += p[len(p.rstrip()):]
        out.append(lead + rendered)
        changed = True
    return ''.join(out), changed

--- rtk filters and compresses command outputs before they reach your LLM context. Single Rust binary, 100+ supported commands, <10ms overhead. ## Token Savings (30-min Claude Code Session) | Operation | Frequency | Standard | rtk | Savings | |-----------|-----------|----------|-----|---------| | `ls` / `tree` | 10x | 2,000 | 400 | -80% | | `cat` / `read` | 20x | 40,000 | 12,000 | -70% | | `grep` / `rg` | 8x | 16,000 | 3,200 | -80% | | `git status` | 10x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% | | `git diff` | 5x | 10,000 | 2,500 | -75% | | `git log` | 5x | 2,500 | 500 | -80% | | `git add/commit/push` | 8x | 1,600 | 120 | -92% | | `cargo test` / `npm test` | 5x | 25,000 | 2,500 | -90% | | `ruff check` | 3x | 3,000 | 600 | -80% | | `pytest` | 4x | 8,000 | 800 | -90% | | `go test` | 3x | 6,000 | 600 | -90% | | `docker ps` | 3x | 900 | 180 | -80% | | **Total** | | **~118,000** | **~23,900** | **-80%** | > Estimates based on medium-sized TypeScript/Rust projects. Actual savings vary by project size. ## Installation ### Homebrew (recommended) ```bash brew install rtk ``` ### Quick Install (Linux/macOS) ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh ``` > Installs to `~/.local/bin`. Add to PATH if needed: > ```bash > echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.bashrc # or ~/.zshrc > ``` ### Cargo ```bash cargo install --git https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk ``` ### Pre-built Binaries Download from [releases](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk/releases): - macOS: `rtk-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` - Linux: `rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` / `rtk-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` - Windows: `rtk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` > **Windows users**: Extract the zip and place `rtk.exe` somewhere in your PATH (e.g. `C:\Users\\.local\bin`). Run RTK from **Command Prompt**, **PowerShell**, or **Windows Terminal** — do not double-click the `.exe` (it will flash and close). For the best experience, use [WSL](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install) where the full hook system works natively. See [Windows setup](#windows) below for details. ### Verify Installation ```bash rtk --version # Should show "rtk 0.28.2" rtk gain # Should show token savings stats ``` > **Name collision warning**: Another project named "rtk" (Rust Type Kit) exists on crates.io. If `rtk gain` fails, you have the wrong package. Use `cargo install --git` above instead. ## Quick Start ```bash # 1. Install for your AI tool rtk init -g # Claude Code / Copilot (default) rtk init -g --gemini # Gemini CLI rtk init -g --codex # Codex (OpenAI) rtk init -g --agent cursor # Cursor rtk init --agent windsurf # Windsurf rtk init --agent cline # Cline / Roo Code rtk init --agent kilocode # Kilo Code rtk init --agent antigravity # Google Antigravity rtk init --agent hermes # Hermes # 2. Restart your AI tool, then test git status # Automatically rewritten to rtk git status ``` Hook-based agents rewrite Bash commands (e.g., `git status` -> `rtk git status`) before execution. Plugin-based agents, including Hermes, use their plugin API to rewrite commands before execution. The agent receives compact output without needing to call `rtk` explicitly. **Important:** the hook only runs on Bash tool calls. Claude Code built-in tools like `Read`, `Grep`, and `Glob` do not pass through the Bash hook, so they are not auto-rewritten. To get RTK's compact output for those workflows, use shell commands (`cat`/`head`/`tail`, `rg`/`grep`, `find`) or call `rtk read`, `rtk grep`, or `rtk find` directly. ## How It Works ``` Without rtk: With rtk: Claude --git status--> shell --> git Claude --git status--> RTK --> git ^ | ^ | | | ~2,000 tokens (raw) | | ~200 tokens | filter | +-----------------------------------+ +------- (filtered) ---+----------+ ``` Four strategies applied per command type: 1. **Smart Filtering** - Removes noise (comments, whitespace, boilerplate) 2. **Grouping** - Aggregates similar items (files by directory, errors by type) 3. **Truncation** - Keeps relevant context, cuts redundancy 4. **Deduplication** - Collapses repeated log lines with counts ## Commands ### Files ```bash rtk ls . # Token-optimized directory tree rtk read file.rs # Smart file reading rtk read file.rs -l aggressive # Signatures only (strips bodies) rtk smart file.rs # 2-line heuristic code summary rtk find "*.rs" . # Compact find results rtk grep "pattern" . # Grouped search results rtk diff file1 file2 # Condensed diff ``` ### Git ```bash rtk git status # Compact status rtk git log -n 10 # One-line commits rtk git diff # Condensed diff rtk git add # -> "ok" rtk git commit -m "msg" # -> "ok abc1234" rtk git push # -> "ok main" rtk git pull # -> "ok 3 files +10 -2" ``` ### GitHub CLI ```bash rtk gh pr list # Compact PR listing rtk gh pr view 42 # PR details + checks rtk gh issue list # Compact issue listing rtk gh run list # Workflow run status ``` ### Test Runners ```bash rtk jest # Jest compact (failures only) rtk vitest # Vitest compact (failures only) rtk playwright test # E2E results (failures only) rtk pytest # Python tests (-90%) rtk go test # Go tests (NDJSON, -90%) rtk cargo test # Cargo tests (-90%) rtk rake test # Ruby minitest (-90%) rtk rspec # RSpec tests (JSON, -60%+) rtk err # Filter errors only from any command rtk test # Generic test wrapper - failures only (-90%) ``` ### Build & Lint ```bash rtk lint # ESLint grouped by rule/file rtk lint biome # Supports other linters rtk tsc # TypeScript errors grouped by file rtk next build # Next.js build compact rtk prettier --check . # Files needing formatting rtk cargo build # Cargo build (-80%) rtk cargo clippy # Cargo clippy (-80%) rtk ruff check # Python linting (JSON, -80%) rtk golangci-lint run # Go linting (JSON, -85%) rtk rubocop # Ruby linting (JSON, -60%+) ``` ### Package Managers ```bash rtk pnpm list # Compact dependency tree rtk pip list # Python packages (auto-detect uv) rtk pip outdated # Outdated packages rtk bundle install # Ruby gems (strip Using lines) rtk prisma generate # Schema generation (no ASCII art) ``` ### AWS ```bash rtk aws sts get-caller-identity # One-line identity rtk aws ec2 describe-instances # Compact instance list rtk aws lambda list-functions # Name/runtime/memory (strips secrets) rtk aws logs get-log-events # Timestamped messages only rtk aws cloudformation describe-stack-events # Failures first rtk aws dynamodb scan # Unwraps type annotations rtk aws iam list-roles # Strips policy documents rtk aws s3 ls # Truncated with tee recovery ``` ### Containers ```bash rtk docker ps # Compact container list rtk docker images # Compact image list rtk docker logs # Deduplicated logs rtk docker compose ps # Compose services rtk kubectl pods # Compact pod list rtk kubectl logs # Deduplicated logs rtk kubectl services # Compact service list ``` ### Data & Analytics ```bash rtk json config.json # Structure without values rtk deps # Dependencies summary rtk env -f AWS # Filtered env vars rtk log app.log # Deduplicated logs rtk curl # Truncate + save full output rtk wget # Download, strip progress bars

def rewrite_one(text):
    """Rewrite the first executable word of shell command segments."""
    # Split on shell operators while preserving separators and quoting.
    # Pipes are part of the first shell command's argument stream from RTK's
    # perspective: only the command before a pipe is rewritten. Boolean and
    # statement separators begin independent commands.
    pieces = re.split(r'((?:&&|\|\||;\s*))', text)
    changed = False
    out = []
    for p in pieces:
        if not p or re.fullmatch(r'(?:&&|\|\||[;|]\s*)', p):
            out.append(p); continue
        lead = p[:len(p)-len(p.lstrip())]
        body = p[len(lead):]
        # Keep leading assignments and environment wrappers intact.
        try:
            toks = shlex.split(body, posix=True)
        except ValueError:
            toks = body.split()
        if not toks:
            out.append(p); continue
        n = 0
        prefix = []

        if n >= len(toks):
